title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
subtitle: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems
description: Data is at the center of many challenges in system design today. Difficult issues need to be figured out, such as scalability, consistency, reliability, efficiency, and maintainability. In this practical and comprehensive guide, author Martin Kleppmann helps you navigate this diverse landscape by examining the pros and cons of various technologies for processing and storing data. Software keeps changing, but the fundamental principles remain the same. With this book, software engineers and architects will learn how to apply those ideas in practice, and how to make full use of data in modern applications. Peer under the hood of the systems you already use, and learn how to use and operate them more effectively.

title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow
subtitle: Concepts, Tools, and Techniques to Build Intelligent Systems
description: Through a series of recent breakthroughs, deep learning has boosted the entire field of machine learning. Now, even programmers who know close to nothing about this technology can use simple, efficient tools to implement programs capable of learning from data. This practical book shows you how. By using concrete examples, minimal theory, and two production-ready Python frameworks—Scikit-Learn and TensorFlow—author Aurélien Géron helps you gain an intuitive understanding of the concepts and tools for building intelligent systems. You’ll learn a range of techniques, starting with simple linear regression and progressing to deep neural networks.

title: Clean Code
subtitle: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
description: Even bad code can function. But if code isn’t clean, it can bring a development organization to its knees. Every year, countless hours and significant resources are lost because of poorly written code. But it doesn’t have to be that way. Noted software expert Robert C. Martin presents a revolutionary paradigm with Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship. Martin has teamed up with his colleagues from Object Mentor to distill their best agile practice of cleaning code ‘on the fly’ into a book that will instill within you the values of a software craftsman and make you a better programmer.

title: Deep Learning
subtitle: Adaptive Computation and Machine Learning series
authors: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville
description: Deep learning is a form of machine learning that enables computers to learn from experience and understand the world in terms of a hierarchy of concepts. Because the computer gathers knowledge from experience, there is no need for a human computer operator to formally specify all the knowledge that the computer needs. The hierarchy of concepts allows the computer to learn complicated concepts by building them out of simpler ones; a graph of these hierarchies would be many layers deep. This book introduces a broad range of topics in deep learning, covering mathematical and conceptual background, deep learning techniques used in industry, and research perspectives.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
subtitle: Global Edition
description: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach offers the most comprehensive, up-to-date introduction to the theory and practice of artificial intelligence. Number one in its field, this textbook is ideal for one or two-semester, undergraduate or graduate-level courses in Artificial Intelligence. The 4th Edition brings readers up to date on the latest technologies, presents concepts in a more unified manner, and offers new or expanded coverage of machine learning, deep learning, transfer learning, multiagent systems, robotics, natural language processing, causality, probabilistic programming, privacy, fairness, and safe AI.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
subtitle: From Journeyman to Master
description: Straight from the programming trenches, The Pragmatic Programmer cuts through the increasing specialization and technicalities of modern software development to examine the core process—taking a requirement and producing working, maintainable code that delights its users. It covers topics ranging from personal responsibility and career development to architectural techniques for keeping your code flexible and easy to adapt and reuse. Written as a series of self-contained sections and filled with entertaining anecdotes, thoughtful examples, and interesting analogies, The Pragmatic Programmer illustrates the best practices and major pitfalls of many different aspects of software development.

title: Dune
subtitle: The Epic Sci-Fi Masterpiece
description: Set on the desert planet Arrakis, Dune is the story of the boy Paul Atreides, heir to a noble family tasked with ruling an inhospitable world where the only thing of value is the 'spice' melange, a drug capable of extending life and enhancing consciousness. Coveted across the known universe, melange is a prize worth fighting for. When House Atreides is betrayed, the destruction of Paul's family will set into motion a journey toward a destiny larger than he could ever have imagined.

title: Neuromancer
subtitle: The Sprawl Trilogy
description: The matrix is a consensus hallucination experienced daily by billions of legitimate operators, in every nation... Case was the sharpest data-thief in the matrix—until he crossed the wrong people and they burned his nervous system with a fungal toxin. Now a charismatic stranger offers him a cure in return for a hack into an unthinkable corporate AI.

title: Foundation
subtitle: Foundation Series Book 1
description: For twelve thousand years the Galactic Empire has ruled supreme. Now it is dying. But only Hari Seldon, creator of the revolutionary science of psychohistory, can see into the future—to a dark age of ignorance, barbarism, and warfare that will last thirty thousand years. To preserve knowledge and save humankind, Seldon gathers the best minds of the Empire and brings them to a bleak planet at the edge of the galaxy.

title: The Three-Body Problem
subtitle: Remembrance of Earth's Past
description: Set against the backdrop of China's Cultural Revolution, a secret military project sends signals into space to establish contact with aliens. An alien civilization on the brink of destruction captures the signal and plans to invade Earth. Meanwhile, on Earth, different camps start forming, planning to either welcome the superior beings and help them take over a world seen as corrupt, or to fight against the invasion.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
subtitle: A Trilogy in Four Parts
description: Seconds before the Earth is demolished to make way for a galactic freeway, Arthur Dent is plucked off the planet by his friend Ford Prefect, a researcher for the revised edition of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Together this dynamic pair begin a journey through space aided by quotes from The Hitchhiker's Guide and a galaxy-full of fellow travelers.

subtitle: A Dystopian Classic
description: Winston Smith toes the Party line, rewriting history to satisfy the Ministry of Truth. With each lie he writes, Winston grows to hate the Party that seeks power for its own sake and persecutes those who dare to commit thoughtcrimes. But as he starts to think for himself, Winston cannot escape the fact that Big Brother is always watching.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
subtitle: Harper Lee Classics
description: The unforgettable novel of a childhood in a sleepy Southern town and the crisis of conscience that rocked it. Compassionate, dramatic, and deeply moving, To Kill A Mockingbird takes readers to the roots of human behavior—to innocence and experience, kindness and cruelty, love and hatred, humor and pathos.

title: The Great Gatsby
subtitle: F. Scott Fitzgerald Definitive Edition
description: The Great Gatsby, F. Scott Fitzgerald's third book, stands as the supreme achievement of his career. First published in 1925, this quintessential novel of the Jazz Age has been acclaimed by generations of readers. The story of the mysteriously wealthy Jay Gatsby and his unrequited love for the beautiful Daisy Buchanan is an exquisitely crafted tale of America in the 1920s.

title: Brave New World
subtitle: Modern Classics Edition
description: Aldous Huxley's profoundly important classic of world literature, Brave New World is a searching vision of an unequal, technologically-advanced future where humans are genetically bred, socially indoctrinated, and pharmaceutically anesthetized to passively uphold an authoritarian ruling order.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
subtitle: Harper Perennial Modern Classics
description: The brilliant, bestselling, landmark novel that tells the story of the Buendía family, and chronicles the irreconcilable conflict between the desire for solitude and the need for love—in rich, imaginative magical realism that defined world literature.

title: The Alchemist
subtitle: A Fable About Following Your Dream
description: Paulo Coelho's masterpiece tells the mystical story of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who yearns to travel in search of a worldly treasure. His quest will lead him to riches far different—and far more satisfying—than he ever imagined.

title: Atomic Habits
subtitle: An Easy & Proven Way to Build Good Habits & Break Bad Ones
description: No matter your goals, Atomic Habits offers a proven framework for improving—every day. James Clear, one of the world's leading experts on habit formation, reveals practical strategies that will teach you exactly how to form good habits, break bad ones, and master the tiny behaviors that lead to remarkable results.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
subtitle: The International Bestseller
description: In the international bestseller, Thinking, Fast and Slow, Daniel Kahneman, the renowned psychologist and winner of the Nobel Prize in Economics, takes us on a groundbreaking tour of the mind and explains the two systems that drive the way we think. System 1 is fast, intuitive, and emotional; System 2 is slower, more deliberative, and more logical.

title: The Psychology of Money
subtitle: Timeless Lessons on Wealth, Greed, and Happiness
description: Doing well with money isn’t necessarily about what you know. It’s about how you behave. And behavior is hard to teach, even to really smart people. Money—investing, personal finance, and business decisions—is typically taught as a math-based field, where data and formulas tell us exactly what to do. But in the real world people don’t make financial decisions on a spreadsheet.

title: Zero to One
subtitle: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future
description: If you want to build a better future, you must believe in secrets. The great secret of our time is that there are still uncharted frontiers to explore and new inventions to create. In Zero to One, legendary entrepreneur and investor Peter Thiel shows how we can find singular ways to create those new things.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
subtitle: A Landmark History
description: From a renowned historian comes a groundbreaking narrative of humanity’s creation and evolution—a #1 international bestseller—that explores the ways in which biology and history have defined us and enhanced our understanding of what it means to be human.

title: Deep Work
subtitle: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World
description: One of the most valuable skills in our economy is becoming increasingly rare. If you master this skill, you'll achieve extraordinary results. Deep work is the ability to focus without distraction on a cognitively demanding task. It's a skill that allows you to quickly master complicated information and produce better results in less time.

title: A Brief History of Time
subtitle: From the Big Bang to Black Holes
description: A landmark volume in science writing by one of the great minds of our time, Stephen Hawking’s book explores such profound questions as: How did the universe begin—and what made its start possible? Does time always flow forward? Is the universe unending—or are there boundaries? Are there other dimensions in space? What will happen when it all ends?

title: Cosmos
subtitle: The Story of Cosmic Evolution, Science and Civilization
description: The magnificent story of fifteen billion years of cosmic evolution transforming matter and life into consciousness, of how science and civilization grew up together, and of the forces and individuals that helped shape modern science. A brilliant exploration of universe and humanity.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
subtitle: The Fates of Human Societies
description: In this 'artful, informative, and delightful' (William H. McNeill, New York Review of Books) book, Jared Diamond convincingly argues that geographical and environmental factors shaped the modern world. Societies that had a head start in food production advanced beyond the hunter-gatherer stage, and then developed religion—as well as nasty germs and potent weapons of war.

title: Meditations
subtitle: A New Translation with Introduction and Notes
description: A series of personal writings by Marcus Aurelius, Roman Emperor from 161 to 180 AD, recording his private notes to himself and ideas on Stoic philosophy. Marcus Aurelius wrote the 12 books of the Meditations as a source for his own guidance and self-improvement.

title: Python Crash Course
subtitle: A Hands-On, Project-Based Introduction to Programming
description: Python Crash Course is a fast-paced, thorough introduction to Python that will have you writing programs, solving problems, and making things that work in no time. In the first half of the book, you’ll learn basic programming concepts, such as variables, lists, classes, and loops, and practice writing clean code. In the second half, you’ll put your new knowledge into practice with three projects.

title: Introduction to Algorithms
subtitle: Third Edition
authors: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein
description: Some books on algorithms are rigorous but incomplete; others cover masses of material but lack rigor. Introduction to Algorithms uniquely combines rigor and comprehensiveness. The book covers a broad range of algorithms in depth, yet makes their design and analysis accessible to all levels of readers. Each chapter is relatively self-contained and can be used as a unit of study.

title: Pride and Prejudice
subtitle: Penguin Classics Deluxe Edition
description: Few have failed to be charmed by the witty and independent Elizabeth Bennet in Austen's beloved classic Pride and Prejudice. When Elizabeth Bennet first meets eligible bachelor Fitzwilliam Darcy, she thinks him arrogant and conceited; he is indifferent to her good looks and lively mind. When she later discovers that Darcy has involved himself in the troubled relationship between his friend Bingley and her beloved sister Jane, she is determined to dislike him more than ever.

title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
subtitle: Second Edition (MIT Electrical Engineering and Computer Science)
authors: Harold Abelson, Gerald Jay Sussman, Julie Sussman
description: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs has had a dramatic impact on computer science curricula over the past three decades. This classic book uses the Scheme programming language to explain the fundamental principles of computation, recursion, data abstraction, and interpreter design.

title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
subtitle: The Gang of Four Classic
authors: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides
description: Capturing a wealth of experience about the design of object-oriented software, four top-notch designers present a catalog of simple and succinct solutions to commonly occurring design problems. 23 foundational patterns that every software engineer must know.

title: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code
subtitle: Second Edition with JavaScript Examples
description: For more than twenty years, serious programmers have relied on Martin Fowler's Refactoring to improve the design of existing code and enhance software maintainability. This completely revised edition shows how to make code simpler, cleaner, and easier to comprehend without changing observable behavior.

title: Cracking the Coding Interview
subtitle: 189 Programming Questions and Solutions
description: Learn how to uncover the hints and hidden details in questions, discover how to break problems down into manageable chunks, and master algorithm design techniques across arrays, trees, graphs, dynamic programming, and system design.

title: Site Reliability Engineering
subtitle: How Google Runs Production Systems
authors: Niall Richard Murphy, Betsy Beyer, Chris Jones, Jennifer Petoff
description: In this collection of essays and articles, key members of Google's Site Reliability Engineering team explain how and why their commitment to the entire lifecycle has enabled the company to successfully build, deploy, monitor, and maintain some of the largest software systems in the world.

title: Fluent Python
subtitle: Clear, Concise, and Effective Programming
description: Don't waste time trying to bend Python to fit patterns you learned in other languages. Python's simplicity lets you become productive quickly, but this often means you aren't using everything it has to offer. With this updated hands-on guide, you'll learn how to write effective, modern Python 3 code by leveraging its best features.

title: Effective Java
subtitle: Third Edition
description: The definitive guide to Java platform best practices—updated for Java 7, 8, and 9. Joshua Bloch provides eighty-five best-practice solutions for the programming challenges you encounter every day, from generics and lambdas to streams, serialization, and concurrency.

title: Grokking Algorithms
subtitle: An Illustrated Guide for Programmers and Other Curious People
description: Grokking Algorithms is a friendly, fully illustrated guide that teaches you how to apply common algorithms to practical problems face-to-face. You'll start with sorting and searching and, as you build up your skills in thinking algorithmically, you'll tackle more complex problems such as data compression and artificial intelligence.

title: Domain-Driven Design
subtitle: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software
description: This is not a book about specific technologies. It offers readers a systematic approach to domain-driven design, presenting an extensive set of modeling best practices, experience-based techniques, and fundamental principles that facilitate the development of software projects facing complex domains.

title: Building Microservices
subtitle: Designing Fine-Grained Systems (Second Edition)
description: As organizations shift from monolithic applications to smaller, self-contained microservices, software architecture is undergoing a revolution. In this second edition, Sam Newman provides a firm grounding in the concepts while diving deep into the latest practices for designing, integrating, testing, and deploying microservices.

title: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
subtitle: Seventh Edition
authors: James F. Kurose, Keith W. Ross
description: Motivates readers by introducing networking through the layered application perspective, providing a top-down, real-world context for learning internet protocols, network architectures, and transport layers.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring
subtitle: The Lord of the Rings: Part One
description: One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all and in the darkness bind them. The first volume in J.R.R. Tolkien's epic masterpiece, recounting the gathering of the fellowship and the perilous quest toward Mordor to destroy the One Ring.

title: The Hobbit
subtitle: There and Back Again
description: Bilbo Baggins is a hobbit who enjoys a comfortable, unambitious life, rarely traveling any farther than his pantry or cellar. But his contentment is disturbed when the wizard Gandalf and a company of dwarves arrive on his doorstep one day to whisk him away on an adventure.

title: A Game of Thrones
subtitle: A Song of Ice and Fire: Book One
description: Summers span decades. Winter can last a lifetime. And the struggle for the Iron Throne has begun. It will stretch from the south, where heat breeds plots, lusts and intrigues; to the vast and savage eastern lands; all the way to the frozen north, where an 800-foot wall of ice protects the kingdom.

title: Ender's Game
subtitle: The Ender Quintet
description: In order to develop a secure defense against a hostile alien race's next attack, government agencies breed child geniuses and train them as soldiers. A young boy, Andrew 'Ender' Wiggin, lives with his kind but distant parents, his sadistic brother Peter, and the person he loves more than anyone else, his sister Valentine.

title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
subtitle: The Inspiration for Blade Runner
description: By 2021, the World War has killed millions, driving entire species into extinction and sending mankind off-planet. Those who remained coveted any living creature, and for people who couldn't afford one, companies built incredibly realistic simulacra: androids. Rick Deckard is an officially sanctioned bounty hunter tasked with finding rogue Nexus-6 androids.

title: Hyperion
subtitle: The Hyperion Cantos Book 1
description: On the world called Hyperion, beyond the reach of galactic law, waits a creature called the Shrike. There are those who worship it. There are those who fear it. And there are those who have vowed to destroy it. On the eve of Armageddon, seven pilgrims set forth on a final voyage to Hyperion seeking the answers to the unsolved riddles of their lives.

title: Snow Crash
subtitle: A Novel
description: In reality, Hiro Protagonist delivers pizza for Uncle Enzo's CosoNostra Pizza Inc., but in the Metaverse he's a warrior prince. Plunging headlong into the enigma of a new computer virus that's striking down hackers everywhere, he races along the neon-lit streets on a search-and-destroy mission for the shadowy virtual villain.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
subtitle: Hainish Cycle
description: A groundbreaking work of science fiction, The Left Hand of Darkness tells the story of a lone human emissary to Winter, an alien world whose inhabitants can choose and change their gender. His goal is to facilitate Winter's inclusion in a growing intergalactic civilization, but to do so he must bridge deep cultural divides.

title: Fahrenheit 451
subtitle: A Novel
description: Guy Montag is a fireman. His job is to destroy the most illegal of commodities, the printed book, along with the houses in which they are hidden. Montag never questions the destruction and ruin his actions produce, until he meets an eccentric young neighbor who introduces him to a past where people didn't live in fear.

title: Solaris
subtitle: The Definitive English Edition
description: When Kris Kelvin arrives at the planet Solaris to study the ocean that covers its surface, he finds a mysterious, living sentient entity that probes the deepest memories and guilts of the human researchers stationed above it.

title: I, Robot
subtitle: The Robot Series
description: The Three Laws of Robotics: 1) A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm. 2) A robot must obey orders given it by human beings except where such orders would conflict with the First Law. 3) A robot must protect its own existence as long as such protection does not conflict with the First or Second Law.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
subtitle: Space Odyssey Series
description: Written concurrently with Stanley Kubrick's cinematic masterpiece, Clarke's novel follows human evolution from ape-ancestors through the lunar discovery of a black monolith, and a voyage toward Saturn aboard the spaceship Discovery steered by the AI computer HAL 9000.

title: Crime and Punishment
subtitle: Translated by David McDuff
description: Raskolnikov, an impoverished student living in the slums of Saint Petersburg, conceives of himself as an extraordinary young man freed from common moral constraints. He murders a pawnbroker and finds himself in an agonizing psychological duel with magistrate Porfiry Petrovich.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
subtitle: A Novel in Four Parts with Epilogue
description: Dostoevsky's final masterpiece is a passionate philosophical novel that enters deeply into the ethical debates of God, free will, morality, and family through the turbulent lives of three Russian brothers.

title: War and Peace
subtitle: Vintage Classics Edition
description: Tolstoy's panoramic masterwork portrays Napoleon's 1812 invasion of Russia and follows five aristocratic families through the horrors of battlefield combat, the splendors of Moscow society, and the search for personal spiritual redemption.

title: Anna Karenina
subtitle: Translated by Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky
description: Acclaimed as the pinnacle of realist fiction, Anna Karenina unfolds against the backdrop of 19th-century imperial Russian society as the aristocratic Anna embarks on a tragic affair with Count Vronsky, while landowner Levin seeks quiet purpose.

title: Wuthering Heights
subtitle: Penguin Classics
description: Lockwood, the new tenant of Thrushcross Grange on the bleak Yorkshire moors, is forced to seek shelter one night at Wuthering Heights, the home of his landlord Heathcliff. There he discovers the history of the tempestuous events that took place years before.

title: Jane Eyre
subtitle: An Autobiography
description: Orphaned as a child, Jane Eyre must overcome poverty and cruelty to forge her own independent path as a governess at Thornfield Hall, where she falls in love with the brooding, enigmatic Mr. Rochester only to discover a devastating secret.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
subtitle: Classic Edition
description: Holden Caulfield's iconic first-person account of the days following his expulsion from Pencey Prep school in Pennsylvania. Wandering through New York City, Holden observes the hypocrisy and phoniness of the adult world.

title: Les Misérables
subtitle: Unabridged Translation
description: The monumental epic of ex-convict Jean Valjean's struggle for redemption amidst the social turbulence of post-revolutionary France, pursued relentlessly by police inspector Javert, while young revolutionaries man the Paris barricades.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
subtitle: The 1891 Expanded Edition
description: Enthralled by his own exquisite portrait, youthful Dorian Gray makes a Faustian pledge that the painting will age and bear the marks of his sins while he maintains untouched physical youth, leading him down a spiral of aesthetic hedonism.

title: Don Quixote
subtitle: Translated by Edith Grossman
description: Widely regarded as the first modern novel, Cervantes' masterpiece tells the hilarious and poignant story of an eccentric Spanish nobleman who becomes convinced he is a knight errant, setting out with his loyal squire Sancho Panza to right the world's wrongs.

title: The Odyssey
subtitle: Translated by Robert Fagles
description: The epic tale of Odysseus' ten-year journey home to Ithaca after the fall of Troy, confronting mythical monsters, enchantresses, and vengeful gods, while his loyal wife Penelope fends off treacherous suitors.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
subtitle: Penguin Classics Unabridged
description: Falsely accused of treason on the eve of his wedding, young sailor Edmond Dantès is imprisoned in the island fortress of the Château d'If. After escaping and finding a legendary buried treasure, he returns to Paris as the mysterious Count of Monte Cristo to exact meticulous revenge.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
subtitle: An Introduction to Logotherapy
description: Psychiatrist Viktor Frankl's memoir of his experiences in Auschwitz and Dachau, coupled with his development of logotherapy—the belief that human beings are fundamentally driven not by pleasure or power, but by the pursuit of meaning.

title: Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience
subtitle: Harper Perennial Modern Classics
description: Legendary psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi's famous investigations of optimal experience reveal that what makes an experience genuinely satisfying is a state of consciousness called flow—intense absorption and joyful engagement where one's skills meet high challenges.

title: Grit: The Power of Passion and Perseverance
subtitle: The #1 New York Times Bestseller
description: Pioneering psychologist Angela Duckworth shows that the secret to outstanding achievement is not innate talent, but a special blend of passion and persistence she calls 'grit.' Packed with insights from West Point cadets, National Spelling Bee finalists, and top educators.

title: Quiet
subtitle: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can't Stop Talking
description: At least one-third of the people we know are introverts. They are the ones who prefer listening to speaking; who innovate and create but dislike self-promotion; who favor working on their own over working in teams. Susan Cain passionately argues that we dramatically undervalue introverts.

title: Essentialism
subtitle: The Disciplined Pursuit of Less
description: Have you ever found yourself stretched too thin? Essentialism isn't about how to get more things done; it's about how to get the right things done. It doesn't mean just doing less for the sake of less either. It is about making the wisest possible investment of your time and energy.

title: Mindset: The New Psychology of Success
subtitle: How We Can Learn to Fulfill Our Potential
description: World-renowned Stanford University psychologist Carol S. Dweck discovers that success in school, work, sports, the arts, and almost every area of human endeavor is influenced by how we think about our talents and abilities: having a fixed mindset versus a growth mindset.

title: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
subtitle: Revised Edition
description: Influence, the classic book on persuasion, explains the psychology of why people say 'yes'—and how to apply these understandings. Dr. Robert Cialdini is the seminal expert in the rapidly expanding field of influence and persuasion, identifying six universal principles.

title: The Lean Startup
subtitle: How Today's Entrepreneurs Use Continuous Innovation to Create Radically Successful Businesses
description: Most startups fail. But many of those failures are preventable. The Lean Startup is a new approach being adopted across the globe, changing the way companies are built and new products are launched through validated learning, rapid experimentation, and the Build-Measure-Learn feedback loop.

title: Good to Great
subtitle: Why Some Companies Make the Leap and Others Don't
description: Can a good company become a great company and, if so, how? Over five years, Jim Collins and his research team analyzed twenty-eight companies, discovering the key concepts that distinguish enduring greatness: Level 5 Leadership, the Hedgehog Concept, and the Flywheel Effect.

title: Principles: Life and Work
subtitle: The #1 New York Times Bestseller
description: Ray Dalio, one of the world's most successful investors and entrepreneurs, shares the unconventional principles that he's developed, refined, and used over the past forty years to create unique results in both life and business at Bridgewater Associates.

title: Freakonomics
subtitle: A Rogue Economist Explores the Hidden Side of Everything
authors: Steven D. Levitt, Stephen J. Dubner
description: Which is more dangerous, a gun or a swimming pool? What do schoolteachers and sumo wrestlers have in common? Levitt and Dubner show that economics is, at root, the study of incentives—how people get what they want, or need, especially when other people want or need the same thing.

title: Bad Blood
subtitle: Secrets and Lies in a Silicon Valley Startup
description: The full inside story of the breathtaking rise and shocking collapse of Theranos, the multibillion-dollar biotech startup founded by Elizabeth Holmes, by the prize-winning journalist who first broke the story and pursued it to the end.

title: Shoe Dog
subtitle: A Memoir by the Creator of Nike
description: Bill Gates named Shoe Dog one of his five favorite books of 2016. In this candid and riveting memoir, Nike founder and board chairman Phil Knight shares the inside story of the company’s early days as an intrepid start-up and its evolution into one of the world's most iconic brands.

title: The Selfish Gene
subtitle: 30th Anniversary Edition
description: Dawkins' brilliant reformulation of the theory of natural selection places the gene, rather than the organism or species, at center stage. He explains how selfish genes generate altruistic behavior, and coined the concept of the meme as a unit of cultural transmission.

title: Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
subtitle: A Metaphorical Fugue on Minds and Machines in the Spirit of Lewis Carroll
description: Winner of the Pulitzer Prize, Hofstadter's tour de force explores the nature of human consciousness and artificial intelligence through the self-referential mathematical theorems of Kurt Gödel, the optical illusions of M.C. Escher, and the contrapuntal music of J.S. Bach.

title: The Elegant Universe
subtitle: Superstrings, Hidden Dimensions, and the Quest for the Ultimate Theory
description: Brian Greene, one of the world's leading string theorists, peels away the layers of mystery surrounding superstring theory to show that all matter and forces in the universe are composed of tiny, vibrating strings of energy operating in eleven dimensions.

title: Six Easy Pieces
subtitle: Essentials of Physics Explained by Its Most Brilliant Teacher
description: Six Easy Pieces introduces the general reader to the most fundamental principles of physics—atoms, basic physics, the relation of physics to other sciences, energy, gravitation, and quantum behavior—distilled from Feynman's legendary Caltech lectures.

title: Silent Spring
subtitle: 40th Anniversary Edition
description: First published in 1962, Silent Spring alerted a large audience to the environmental and human dangers of indiscriminate pesticide use, catalyzing the modern ecological movement and the founding of the EPA.

title: What If?
subtitle: Serious Scientific Answers to Absurd Hypothetical Questions
description: From the creator of the wildly popular webcomic xkcd, hilarious and informative answers to important questions you probably never thought to ask, using ballistics calculations, thermodynamics, and physics models.

title: The Silk Roads
subtitle: A New History of the World
description: An international bestseller and a major reassessment of world history, The Silk Roads shows how the heart of global civilization beat along the ancient arteries connecting East and West, where religions, trade goods, empires, and plagues shaped our destiny.

title: The Lessons of History
subtitle: A Brief Review of Human Civilization
description: A concise survey of the culture and civilization of mankind, concluding the monumental Story of Civilization series. The Pulitzer Prize-winning historians compress five millennia of human triumphs and catastrophes into twelve illuminating essays.

title: A People's History of the United States
subtitle: 1492 to Present
description: A People's History of the United States tells the story of America from the bottom up, centering the voices of Native Americans, enslaved laborers, immigrant factory workers, and women rather than presidents and generals.

title: Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do?
subtitle: A Harvard Course in Philosophy
description: Based on his famous Harvard course, Sandel examines affirmative action, income inequality, military service, and individual rights through the moral lenses of utilitarianism, Immanuel Kant, John Locke, and Aristotle.

title: Beyond Good and Evil
subtitle: Prelude to a Philosophy of the Future
description: Nietzsche dismantles conventional morality, philosophical dogmas, and religious systems, asserting the Will to Power and calling for free spirits to forge their own values beyond naive dualities of good and evil.

title: The Republic
subtitle: Translated by Desmond Lee
description: Plato's central work features Socrates debating justice, the ideal state, the Allegory of the Cave, and the rule of Philosopher Kings, forming the cornerstone of Western political and philosophical thought.

title: The Prince
subtitle: Penguin Classics Deluxe Edition
description: Machiavelli's notorious handbook for Renaissance rulers analyzes political power, fortune, and human nature with ruthless realism, asserting that effective leaders must know how to be feared as well as loved.
